dedupe_keys.name: reducing cascading failure risk by increasing power communication network interdependency

description: This paper compares simple topological models of interdependent networks with models that capture the actual dynamics of cascading failures in power systems coupled to communication networks. In two sets of experiments it first compares topological contagion with a power system cascading model and finds the power grid much more vulnerable, and then compares a topological cascade model of coupled networks with three physics-based models of power grids coupled to communication networks. In all but the most extreme case the physics-based models indicate that increasing power-communication coupling decreases vulnerability, the opposite of the topological result where zero coupling is optimal; an extreme case where communication failures immediately cause grid failures shows that poorly designed coupling can be harmful. The results suggest design strategies for reducing the risk of cascades in interdependent infrastructure. Producer: Korkali, Veneman, Tivnan and Hines, submitted to arXiv in October 2014 and revised in June 2015 (physics and society). Coverage: generic models, not a named country. Access: free PDF on arXiv. Licence and cost: free to read; licence arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence (the paper; no open reuse licence). Caveats: the models are stylised and the abstract does not name the test networks or code. Simulation uses: it is a methodological benchmark for choosing between topological and physics-based cascade models in interdependency studies.
